journeys: Chromium enters the actual synthetic storefront, follows the signed checkout handoff and reviews server-configured delivery rates before placing a COD order.

Chromium completes the hosted online payment path through the real Gateway and a synthetic Razorpay adapter; canonical order, capture, ledger and notification effects are checked against owned Postgres.

After Chromium has reviewed a ₹20 COD quote, the fixture changes the saved rate to ₹25 before Gateway delivery validation. The stale quote returns a conflict, creates no order or payment intent, refreshes the delivery options, and requires explicit selection of the ₹25 amount before exactly one COD order is created.
limits: All identities, products, addresses and orders are synthetic and confined to runner-owned Postgres.
The hosted payment adapter is synthetic test evidence, not a Razorpay sandbox or live transaction.
This is local Chromium/worker/database acceptance, not physical-device, carrier, hosted-deployment or Phase 8 acceptance.
